system.name: ChattyChef
system.one_liner: Study of recipe-grounded instructional dialogue on the new ChattyChef dataset, with auxiliary intent detection and state tracking to fix out-of-order instructions.

content.variant_note: one recipe and four user turns answered by a good and a faulty system in aligned columns, the bad replies tagged with their error type
content.argues: Recipe-grounded replies can go wrong in four ways (irrelevant, wrong order, lack of information, wrong information); a good system answers each turn from the right recipe step.
content.subject: Recipe card plus a four-turn cooking dialogue answered by good System #1 and faulty System #2, errors tagged.

elements.name: Recipe
elements.role: the grounding document the system must follow
elements.drawn_as: light grey card with dashed grey frame, bold title, italic condensed steps and a food photo

elements.name: Step 1 ... Step 5
elements.role: ordered recipe steps; steps 1 and 2 are elided, steps 3 to 5 are written out
elements.drawn_as: italic condensed text lines in the recipe card

elements.name: User
elements.role: the cook who asks what to do next and how long to cook
elements.drawn_as: bold column title next to a chef icon

elements.name: User turns (4 bubbles)
elements.role: four questions: what to do next, what is next, how long to cook, how long for the other side
elements.drawn_as: white speech bubbles with grey outline, tail at top-left

elements.name: System #1
elements.role: the system whose replies are good (no error tags)
elements.drawn_as: dark blue bold column title with a smiling blue robot icon

elements.name: System #1 replies (4 bubbles)
elements.role: correct replies that follow the recipe order and details
elements.drawn_as: light blue speech bubbles with dark blue outline

elements.name: System #2
elements.role: the system whose replies are bad, each tagged with an error type
elements.drawn_as: red bold column title with a red robot icon with x eyes

elements.name: System #2 replies (4 bubbles)

elements.name: Irrelevant

elements.name: Wrong Order

elements.drawn_as: red filled box, white bold text, red arrow into the bubble

elements.name: Lack of Information
elements.role: error type of 'You can cook for 3-4 minutes on one side.' (the other side is missing)
elements.drawn_as: red filled box, white bold text, red arrow into the bubble

elements.name: Wrong Information
elements.role: error type of '5 minutes.' (the recipe says 2-3 minutes)
elements.drawn_as: red filled box, white bold text, red arrow into the bubble

examples.what: a four-turn hash-brown cooking dialogue: 'I have added the butter to the pan. What do I do next?' ... 'Sorry, how long do I need to cook the other side?' with a good and a bad reply to each turn
examples.form: speech bubbles in three aligned columns next to a recipe card with steps

idioms.drawn_as: rounded speech bubbles with a small tail at the top-left, white with grey outline for the user, light blue and light red for the two systems; avatars sit once in each column header, not on every bubble
cartoon robot head whose face carries the verdict: a smile for the good system, x eyes and a wavy mouth for the bad one

content.reading_order: Starts at the recipe card, then the User column, then across each row to the blue reply and the red reply with its tag, down four turns.

layout.arrangement_note: A dashed recipe card with a photo at the far left; to its right three aligned columns of speech bubbles (User white, System #1 blue, System #2 red), one row per turn so every question is answered side by side; a fourth column of red error tags with short arrows sits at the right edge, pinned to System #2's replies.
layout.lanes: 3 aligned columns (User, System #1, System #2) by 4 turn rows, plus a column of error tags

palette.used_for: System #2 title, bubble outlines, arrows and the fill of the error tags (red = bad)
System #1 bubble outlines and title (dark blue)
outlines of the user bubbles and the dashed recipe frame (grey)

style.stroke: 0.75 pt outlines on bubbles and arrows in blue, red or grey; thin dashed grey frame on the recipe card
style.font: sans (Helvetica) 5-7 pt: 6.5 pt bubble text, 7 pt bold column titles, 5 pt bold white tag text; condensed italic for the recipe steps
style.arrows: short red arrows with small filled heads from each error tag into its bubble; no flow arrows

encoding.color_means: Blue = System #1, the good replies; red = System #2, the bad replies and the error tags; white with grey outline = user turns; pale grey with dashed frame = the recipe.
encoding.line_style_means: Dashed frame = the recipe document; solid rounded outlines = utterances.
encoding.shape_means: Speech bubbles with a tail = utterances; robot head = a system, its face tells good from bad; chef icon = the user; solid red rectangles = error types.
encoding.marker_means: Tag words name the error type and a short red arrow pins each tag to its reply; Step 1-5 number the recipe.
encoding.emphasis: The blue versus red split and the red tags carry the message; rows are aligned across the columns so the eye compares good and bad replies turn by turn.
reusable_patterns: two aligned reply columns (good, bad) answering the same user turns
red error-tag boxes pinned to bad replies with short arrows
robot icons with mood faces as column headers
grounding document card with photo at the left of the dialogue
bubble heights fitted to the text so rows stay aligned
weaknesses: 5 pt white-on-red tag text is very small
recipe steps 1 and 2 are elided, so the reader cannot check every reply
no line links a reply to the recipe step it should come from

own: a recipe and a dialogue snippet written out in full

new_tags.name: chat-bubbles
new_tags.what: an exchange drawn as speech bubbles with tails, one column per speaker

new_tags.name: turn-aligned-columns
new_tags.what: one user column and several system columns of bubbles aligned row by row, so every turn is answered side by side

lessons.what_to_learn: Show failure types by running one conversation through a good and a faulty system in aligned columns, pin a short red tag with an arrow to each wrong reply, and colour each system the same on icon, title and bubbles.
lessons.suits: Task or error-analysis figures for dialogue, QA or generation where each failure type can be shown by one short reply.

evidence: A conversation snippet of the cooking instructional dialogue task with good and bad system responses
The incorrect responses are classified into four error types (examples in Figure 1)

summary: The paper studies recipe-grounded conversation, where a dialogue system walks a user through a recipe, and finds that the main failure of a fine-tuned GPT-J is giving instructions in the wrong order; it adds intent detection and instruction state tracking and releases the ChattyChef dataset. Figure 1 sets the task on one hash-brown recipe: a dashed recipe card with a photo on the left, then three aligned columns of speech bubbles for the user's four turns, a good System #1 in blue and a faulty System #2 in red. Red tags with short arrows name the error of each bad reply: Irrelevant, Wrong Order, Lack of Information, Wrong Information. Line-art icons of a cook and two robots head the columns.
summary_zh: 论文研究菜谱对话中的指令顺序问题。图 1 以一份炸薯饼菜谱为例：左侧为带照片的虚线菜谱卡，右侧三列对话气泡依次是用户的四轮提问、正确的 System #1（蓝）和出错的 System #2（红），红色标签标出四类错误。
notes: The preview has blank space above the figure and the first caption line cut off at its bottom edge; neither is part of the figure. The caption says 'good and bad system responses', so System #1 is read as the good one and System #2 as the bad one; whether the bad replies are real model outputs or constructed is not stated (the paper's Table 1 attributes the error types to a fine-tuned GPT-J). Prior labels kept; panels left empty because the recipe card and columns are loose regions of one drawing.
